paper.title: SHARP: A Self-Evolving Human-Auditable Rubric Policy for Financial Trading Agents
paper.central_claim: Replacing free-form prompt optimization with a bounded, human-readable rubric of condition-action rules, evolved by an attribution agent (diagnose worst P&L days, map to rule IDs), atomic rule edits, and a walk-forward validation gate, turns generic initial heuristics into robust out-of-sample trading strategies (10-20 pp average lift for compact models) while keeping the policy auditable.

signatures.object: Analyst rubric: a bounded (<=18) versioned set of IF/THEN rules injected into the LLM analyst prompt; baseline = shared generic initial rubric (6 rules + 1-4 sector rules) and, in A2, a free-form prompt
signatures.information: Attribution agent sees the 20 worst training-period portfolio days with holdings, predicted returns, self-reported activated rules, realized P&L and news; evolution agent sees current rubric + error patterns; validation uses the next held-out month; test months and the future are hidden
signatures.operation: Backtest -> attribute worst days to rubric vulnerabilities (patterns recurring >=3 days) -> propose <=3 atomic rule edits (modify/add/remove) -> apply -> backtest on validation month
signatures.output: Candidate rubric R~; accepted if validation excess return >= best-so-far - 50 bps, best-by-validation rubric kept across J=5 rounds
signatures.conditions: daily long-short equities, 16 stocks per sector, news window 3 days, 5L/5S portfolio, 5 bps cost, open-to-open returns
signatures.feedback: realized P&L of backtest on training days (delayed scalar) plus validation excess return
signatures.selection_rule_data: validation month of each window (single 21-day-ish period) with 0.5 pp tolerance; no paired test; rubric selected by max validation return
signatures.persistence: rubric versions with rule-level diffs; frozen R* used for the 2-month test; evolution restarts from the same R0 in every window
signatures.later_use: daily trading signals on test days via LLM analyst conditioned on the frozen rubric
signatures.claimed_effect: Static -> Evo 3-sector average: GPT-4o-mini +0.6% -> +20.9%, GPT-4.1-mini -4.4% -> +13.4%; Qwen +9.8 pp, Llama +12.9 pp
signatures.failure_boundary: Attribution is LLM self-reported; tail-only (worst 20 days); 3 windows, 7-month regime; slippage/impact omitted; regime-dependent rules need periodic re-evolution

signatures.object: Mutation operator of the improvement loop (atomic rule edits vs free-form prompt rewrite)
signatures.information: same attribution signals in both arms (A2 keeps backbone, attribution, budget and gate identical)
signatures.operation: Constrain candidates to rule-level edits with a hard rule cap and <=3 mutations per round
signatures.claimed_effect: A2 free reflection AI Tech 4o -12.1% vs full +33.2%; 4.1-mini +6.0% vs +22.9%
signatures.failure_boundary: single sector, two backbones, no repeats

gap.author_gap: Unbounded free-form prompt mutation under noisy, delayed P&L cannot attribute losses to localized logic, causing untargeted rewrites and policy drift.
gap.checked_gap: Real and well scoped for trading: aggregate P&L is a poor localizer. But the claim that structure/attribution rather than other differences fixes it is supported only by in-house ablations A1/A2; the named neighbors (ATLAS, GEPA, MIPRO, OPRO) are not run, and generic rule-list/playbook editing methods (e.g. delta-edit playbooks, ExpeL-style rule stores) are not discussed.

rs_pattern.reason: Opus = sol. The paper's move targets the representation and mutation operator of an iterative optimizer: a free-text prompt rewritten wholesale becomes a bounded set of condition–action rules edited atomically. That operator was conventionally fixed in prompt-optimization loops, and here it is treated as a design variable. son55's structural_prior_encoding is not kept (son55 itself rated it weak): no known invariant of the market is encoded, and locality of edits is an interface choice, not a symmetry or topology prior.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In three short walk-forward windows per sector, a frozen rubric evolved by LLM attribution and gated on a held-out month produced higher out-of-sample long-short returns than the same LLM with the initial rubric (author-reported, single run).
assessment.not_supported: Statistical reliability; superiority over ATLAS/GEPA-style optimizers or over the best LLM baseline; reliability of the self-reported rule attribution; live trading viability; cross-window or cross-regime retention.
unresolved: Opus: the 'remaining baselines negligible' prose is contradicted by Table 1 (opus:O01).
assessment.note: Author-reported numbers only; not reproduced. Improver level not claimed (the improver is not itself edited).

G.reason: Both seats 3, confirmed. The bottleneck is concrete: credit assignment for free-form prompt optimizers under noisy, delayed P&L. Named neighbours are ATLAS/OPRO, FinCon and GEPA/MIPRO, and the failure is reproduced in-paper (A2). Not 4: the prompt-optimizer neighbours are not run, and 'inevitably leading to drift' is over-general.

M.reason: Both seats 3, confirmed. Rule-ID localisation, cross-sample diagnosis over the 20 worst days with recurrence ≥3, ≤3 atomic edits and a disjoint validation gate are a coherent, distinguishable alternative to whole-prompt rewrites. Weak points: attribution is self-reported and tail-only.

X.reason: Both seats 3, confirmed. Algorithm 1, the cap of 18 rules, ≤3 mutations, ε = 50 bps, K_attr = 20, the rollback rule and frozen deployment are reconstructable. Not 4: the attribution and evolution prompts are not given, the sector-specific initial rules are only in the code, the gate is whole-candidate, and there is no cross-window retention.

E.measurement.reason: Opus = sol, at the run's cap for text–table contradictions. The metrics themselves (O2O returns, Sharpe, MaxDD, Calmar, a 1000-trial cost-aware null) are reconstructable. Problems: (1) costs are charged on entries only for the methods, while the null counts a flip as two trades (sol:E014); (2) slippage and impact are omitted; (3) the comparator LLM baselines are undocumented (opus:O02); (4) §4.2's 'remaining baselines negligible' is contradicted by Table 1 (FinHEAR-4o 11.1%, FinCon-4.1 9.0%; opus:O01).

E.causality.reason: Opus = sol. Static (same backbone, inputs and initial rubric, no evolution) is run on all four backbones: it is below Evo in all 6 sector cells for the two OpenAI backbones and in both open-model 3-sector averages. A2 is a purpose-built alternative-optimizer arm (free-form rewrite with identical init, budget and gate), and A1 removes attribution. Not 4: the ablations are on AI Tech only (the best sector), there is no gate-off arm, and the named optimizer neighbours are not run. son55's single-run point is scored in E.statistics (A2 rule). The regime-fit reading (momentum flip in a rally) is the adaptation mechanism itself, judged out of sample.

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 3, confirmed. Walk-forward windows of 4-month train, 1-month validation and 2-month test, with the rubric frozen at test. Backbone cutoffs predate the data, there is a 23:59 UTC news cutoff, and the news window is chosen on validation. Not 4: one market regime over ~6 months, three windows, no data-overlap audit, and the choice of sector for the ablations is not justified.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 1, confirmed (A2 tier 1). Sample sizes (122 days, three windows), negative cells and a random null are reported, but there are no repeated evolution runs, intervals or tests. The authors disclaim significance.

E.cost.reason: Both seats 2, confirmed. Per-sector wall-clock covers all evolution stages (API about 3h30; 4×H100 about 5h40–6h55). There are no token or dollar totals, no baseline compute, and no matched-budget optimizer comparison beyond A2.
